high.title: After Weaker Inflation, Economists Revise Estimates for 2026; See This Monday's Focus Report (13)
high.summary: The Banco Central do Brasil's weekly Focus Report, released Monday July 13, showed inflation expectations declining for the **second consecutive week** — a meaningful signal of improving market sentiment on the price outlook. The median forecast for Brazil's official inflation index (IPCA) for **2026 was revised down from 5.30% to 5.16%**, following the benign CPI print released on Friday, July 10. Expectations for 2027 edged slightly higher from 4.18% to 4.20%, while 2028 and 2029 remained anchored at 3.70% and 3.50%, respectively.

high.title: War Escalation and Oil Price Surge Pressure Markets; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (13)
high.summary: Markets opened the week in a cautious tone as Middle East tensions escalated sharply over the weekend, with the United States and Iran exchanging airstrikes after President Donald Trump authorized bombardments against Iranian targets — framed by Washington as retaliation for an Iranian attack on a commercial vessel in the region. Iran subsequently retaliated, ratcheting up geopolitical risk significantly.

medium.title: Trump Contradicts Evidence, Claims Falling Inflation and Oil Prices
medium.summary: President Donald Trump claimed on his Truth Social platform that U.S. prices are falling alongside declining oil and gas quotations — statements that contradict official data. U.S. CPI stood at **4.2% year-over-year in May**, up from 3.8% in April, while the PCE index also remains elevated. This disconnect between White House rhetoric and actual inflation data raises uncertainty around the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory. For Brazil traders, a Fed that is forced to stay higher-for-longer due to persistent U.S. inflation would maintain upward pressure on the USD broadly, keeping BRL under depreciation pressure and limiting room for the BCB to ease the Selic without triggering capital outflows. **Watch:** Upcoming U.S. CPI data releases and Fed communication for clearer direction on the USD/BRL pair.

medium.title: New Pix? Inter's (INTR) Plan to Dominate the Billion-Dollar International Payments Market That Major Banks Are Ignoring
medium.summary: Banco Inter (INTR) is reportedly developing a proprietary infrastructure to facilitate cross-border international payments, targeting a segment that legacy Brazilian banks have largely neglected. The article draws a parallel to the Pix instant payment system — designed by the BCB — which rapidly displaced the older DOC and TED transfer rails. Inter's international payments push could represent a meaningful revenue diversification opportunity and positions the digital bank competitively within Brazil's evolving fintech landscape. While not a direct macro market mover, it is relevant for investors with exposure to Brazilian banking sector equities, particularly those comparing Inter against incumbents like Itaú, Bradesco, and Banco do Brasil on the B3.

medium.title: JPMorgan Beats Projections, But CEO Warns on Geopolitics and Inflation
medium.summary: JPMorgan Chase reported Q2 2026 net income of US$21.16 billion, up 41% year-on-year, with EPS of US$7.70 significantly beating the FactSet consensus of US$5.59. Net revenue surged 28% annually to US$57.35 billion, also well above expectations. Despite the strong headline numbers, CEO Jamie Dimon's explicit warnings about geopolitical risks and inflation are the more market-relevant signal for EM investors. His cautionary tone suggests that global macro uncertainty — including the Middle East conflict and persistent inflation pressures — could constrain risk appetite for emerging market assets including BRL and Brazilian equities. A risk-off tilt from global investors influenced by Dimon's remarks could weigh on capital flows into Brazil, particularly in the short term.

medium.title: Earnings Season for Q2 2026 Is Starting: Key Calendar and Stocks to Watch
medium.summary: Brazil's Q2 2026 earnings season is set to kick off with Neoenergia reporting on July 21, with the busiest period arriving in August — 32 companies are scheduled to report on August 12 alone. JPMorgan's local team has provided expectations for the season, which will be a key driver of Ibovespa direction and sector rotation on B3 in the coming weeks. For fund managers with Brazilian equity exposure, this calendar is important for positioning ahead of results from major index constituents. Strong corporate earnings could provide a positive catalyst for the Ibovespa and indirectly support BRL through improved risk sentiment and potential foreign inflows into Brazilian equities.
